utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm the doctor today. I see you've got burning when you pass urine since yesterday. Tell me a bit more about what's been happening — how it started, and whether you've had anything else like needing to go more often, urgency, blood in the urine, or any pain in your lower tummy?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so it has been about a day and a half now. It stings and burns, worst right at the end of weeing, and I am going constantly—every half hour—and have to rush even though only a little bit comes out. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I have not seen any blood, and I just have that low ache above my bladder and nothing else.

utterance: Thanks. A few important ones: any fever, chills or shakes? Any pain in your back or sides, around the kidneys? Any nausea or vomiting? And is there any chance you could be pregnant — when was your last period, and are you taking the pill regularly?
reply: No, I have not had any fevers or shivers, and nothing in my back either, just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy. I am eating normally and have not been sick, and I do not think there is any chance I could be pregnant since my last period was about two weeks ago and was normal, and I am on the pill and do not miss it.

utterance: Good. You mentioned "UTI again" — how many urine infections have you had before, how recently, and what antibiotics were you given? Did they work? Also, are you sexually active, any new partner recently, and any vaginal discharge, itch or irritation?
reply: I only had one UTI about two years ago, and I have not had any antibiotics this year. I have a boyfriend I have been with for about a year and it is just him, and I have not had any discharge, itch, or irritation.

awards.label: Antibiotics in the last few months

utterance: Do you remember what antibiotic you had last time and whether it worked? Any other medical problems, kidney problems or stones in the past, or any medicines besides the pill? And has there been any chance of a sexually transmitted infection — have you and your boyfriend both been tested?
reply: No, I have not had any kidney problems or stones, I am not on any other medicines besides the pill, and no, we have not been tested for anything like that.

utterance: No worries. Do you use condoms with your boyfriend? And have you tried anything so far — Ural sachets, cranberry, pain relief? Lastly, any family history of kidney problems?
reply: We do not use condoms because I am on the pill, and I have not tried anything so far, and nothing like that runs in my family.

finding: Soft. Mild suprapubic tenderness; non-tender elsewhere. No masses or organomegaly.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: Your urine test confirms a bladder infection (cystitis), and your temperature is normal and your kidneys aren't tender, so it looks like a simple bladder infection rather than something spreading to the kidneys. One more thing: since you and your boyfriend haven't used condoms and neither of you has been tested, I'd recommend we check a urine sample for chlamydia and gonorrhoea today as a routine screen — it's recommended for everyone under 30 who is sexually active, and it can sometimes cause similar symptoms. Are you happy for me to add that?
reply: Can't we just skip that and get the antibiotics? I really just need to get back to work.

utterance: Absolutely, I'll sort the antibiotics right now. The chlamydia test is just done on the same urine sample you've already given — no extra time for you, and the results come back in a couple of days. Chlamydia often causes no symptoms at all, and if it's left untreated it can affect your fertility later, so I'd really recommend it. Is that okay?
reply: Okay, if we can just use the same sample, that is fine.

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
Here's the plan, Chloe:

1. Antibiotic: trimethoprim 300 mg, one tablet at night for 3 nights. Take all three even if you feel better after the first day. It doesn't interfere with your pill.
2. Symptom relief: drink plenty of water, and you can take paracetamol or ibuprofen if the ache or burning is bothering you. Urinary alkaliniser sachets (Ural) from the chemist can help the stinging too. Try to empty your bladder fully and pass urine after sex.
3. You should feel noticeably better within 1–2 days. If you're NOT improving after 48 hours on the antibiotic, or symptoms come back soon after finishing, come back and we'll send a urine sample to the lab to check which antibiotic the bug is sensitive to.
4. Red flags — come back urgently or go to the emergency department if you develop a fever, shivers or shakes, pain in your back or sides, vomiting so you can't keep fluids or tablets down, or if you see a lot of blood in your urine. Those could mean the infection has moved to the kidneys, which needs stronger treatment.
5. The chlamydia/gonorrhoea test result will be back in about 2 days — we'll call you if it needs follow-up; if it's positive you and your boyfriend would both need treatment.
6. You're fine to work, but if you're feeling rotten today I can give you a medical certificate.

Does that all make sense, and do you have any questions?
reply: That makes sense, and I do not need a medical certificate since I can just get straight back to work now.

utterance: Great. Take care, Chloe — remember: finish all three tablets, plenty of fluids, and come back straight away if you get a fever, back pain, or you're not better in two days. We'll be in touch about the test result.
reply: Thanks, I will take the tablets and come back if it does not get better.
